newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEEGAN KEEPS FEET FIRMLY ON GROUND AFTER FAMOUS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEEGAN KEEPS FEET FIRMLY ON GROUND AFTER FAMOUS VICTORY.

text.p: The city of Newcastle awoke after a night of celebration on Monday with a message from Kevin Keegan snapping fans nursing hangovers back to reality.

"We've won nothing yet," said Keegan, a day after Newcastle United demolished champions Manchester United 5-0 in a match already being included in lists of one of the best English leagye matches ever played.
Keegan warned his team's awesome destruction of the champions has done nothing but avenge old wounds and restore faith in his belief that the premier league can be won in cavalier fashion.
"Nothing has been won here in terms of titles," said Keegan, who was celebrating his first league victory over Manchester United since Newcastle returned to the elite division in 1993.
"It's a massive boost for our confidence and a little bit of revenge for the Charity Shield mauling we had at Wembley.
"We looked like a team on a mission. But I'm not going to get carried away by it.
"We have to go to Old Trafford in the second or third last game of the season and they'll look forward to that as much as we will. It will be another classic."

Club chairman Sir John Hall, who has invested tens of millions of pounds to bring the title back to the city for the first time since 1927, insisted: "That was truly championship class -- on this performance we'll be there at the end."
But the lead is only two points over Arsenal, five over United, and nothing like the 12-point advantage they squandered last year.

But now Newcastle have a psychological boost, the goals from Darren Peacock, David Ginola, Les Ferdinand, Alan Shearer and Philippe Albert's exquisite final chip exorcising the jinx United have held over them in recent years.
It gave United their worst drubbing since they slumped 5-0 at Everton on October 27, 1984.

But Keegan, and all their premier league rivals, will recall how a similar scoreline at Tottenham on New Year's Day brought a startling response -- just one domestic defeat in the next 33 games and another cup and league double.
"United won't fritter away," says the Newcastle boss. "They'll be there at the end, along with Liverpool, maybe Arsenal. But I know one thing -- we're going to be in the mixer."

"We are a team worth paying money to watch," he said, acclaiming the performance -- their most prolific since Wimbledon were drubbed 6-1 at St James' Park in the premier league a year ago -- as the best of his managerial life.
"We played the way we know we can -- and I still believe we should have won the League playing this way last season.
"But we're not going to gloat about it. We'll go back on to the training field, work on the defence a bit more, and then we'll go out and try to do the same thing again."
Ferguson has never tasted such a defeat in his managerial life -- 5-1 in the Manchester derby in 1989 was his worst, along with a 4-0 Champions League loss in Barcelona.
But he insists it is, like the loss at White Hart Lane, a blip: "You have to take your medicine and go home -- and we're big enough to do that.
"It's just another day in the history of Manchester United and we'll get over it. We'll be OK, the players know that in many ways it was a false game."
And he added: "I'm pleased with my players after the week they've had, they ran themselves into the ground. But we can have no complaints. We were well beaten."
United had not conceded a goal in five games before Sunday and in the lead-up to the game had beaten Liverpool in the league and Fenerbahce in the Champions League.
And at least their vast army of fans -- some of whom were caught smiling in utter disbelief by TV cameras on Sunday -- have not lost faith.
Andy Walsh, secretary of the Manchester United Independent Supporters Association, insists the defeat was "just a blip."
"This was an aberration that proves that even Manchester United are human," he said.
"We can recognise a great performance by other teams but we're still the greatest team anyone the world has ever seen.
"I don't think United played that badly. Newcastle took their chances and scored some great goals. They were on song and we were off key. But it's only one game."
